name: Just Energy Transition Investment Plan
description: The Just Energy Transition Investment Plan sets out the investments required between 2023-2027 to achieve South Africa's decarbonisation commitments in its NDC (2021). The preamble of the Plan states that it "gives effect" to the Just Energy Transition Partnership agreed at COP26 between South Africa and the governments of France, Germany, United Kingdom, United States and the European Union. The Plan was developed along the Just Transition Framework. The Plan covers the electricity sector, new energy vehicle sector, green hydrogen sector, cross-cutting investments and also sets out policies relating to financing and implementing the Plan.

name: Natural Disaster Management Act, 1998 (No. 21 of 1998)
description: This Act makes provision for measures to better manage the state of calamity caused by a natural disaster. It provides for the establishment of the National Disaster Management Council, the National Disaster Management Office and the National Emergency Operation Centre and for the appointment of the National Disaster Controller, the National Disaster Co-ordinator and the Disaster Service Liaison Officer.

The preamble of the Plan states that it "gives effect" to the Just Energy Transition Partnership agreed at COP26 between South Africa and the governments of France, Germany, United Kingdom, United States and the European Union. name: Zimbabwe Vision 2030
description: Zimbabwe Vision 2030 embodies the aspirations towards a Prosperous Upper Middle-Income Nation by 2030, in line with the Sustainable Development Goals and African Union Agenda 2063. It provides for plans to partner with development partners to “broaden climate change mitigation and adaptation activities to include critical elements such as water management and harvesting measures to mitigate the effects of drought, respect for biodiversity and wetland management issues.”

name: National Climate Agreement (Klimaatakkoord)
description:
The National Climate Agreement builds on the Energy Accord, but rather than focusing solely on energy policy, it addresses all greenhouse gas emissions. In 2023 the emission reduction targets of the National Climate Agreement were further hardened through the Coalition Agreement 2021-2025. In order to achieve these targets, additional measures were introduced in “Sharp targets, sharp choices”, a report one national climate policy for 2030 and 2050, which included the following commitments:
The 2019 agreement set out a strategy to achieve 49% reduction of CO2 emissions by 2030 compared to 1990 levels, and 95% by 2050. The new and hardened target of the National Climate Agreement contains a net zero pledge. The goal is to be climate-neutral by 2050 at the latest, and achieve a 55% reduction in CO2 emissions by 2030 compared to 1990 levels. In order to achieve the ambition for 2030 the target for policy is focused on reducing CO2 emissions by 60% in 2030. To meet this end, the government also presented an additional climate package on the 26th of April, 2023. This includes a €35 billion climate and transition fund for the next 10 years.
Overall, the National Climate Agreement came as a response to the Urgenda case and in parallel to the Climate Act. It details agreements made with the following sectors: electricity, industry, built environment, traffic and transport, and agriculture. The Agreement also introduces a carbon tax, applicable to industry and levied against emissions that exceed the EU ETS Benchmarks (after the deduction of a predefined reduction path). The tax applies to all installations in the EU ETS, as well as waste incinerators and large emitters of non-CO2 GhGs, such as N2). The CO2 tax levy will start at €30/t CO2 in 2021 and will increase each year by €10.56, up to a rate of €125/t CO2 in 2030. The annual additional costs associated with the Climate Agreement are estimated to be less than 0.5% of GDP in 2030.
The National Climate Agreement contains commitments with five sectors on the measures they will take over the next 10 years and beyond to meet climate targets. The following targets are decided upon per sector:

Electricity: in 2030 the Netherlands want 70% of all electricity to come from wind turbines on sea and land, and solar panels on roofs and solar parks. By 2050 the Netherlands wants to be completely free from fossil fuels, like coal and gas 
Industry: by 2050 the industry is circular, and “emits virtually no more greenhouse gases”
Mobility: by 2050 Dutch traffic and all transport will no longer emit harmful exhaust gases and CO2
The built environment: by 2050, 7 million homes and 1 million buildings need to be off natural gas
Agriculture and land-use: by 2050, agriculture and land-use will be climate neutral

name: Public Investment Fund Green Finance Framework
description: The Public Investment Fund (PIF) of Saudi Arabia has established a Green Finance Framework that sets out its strategy for contributing to the achievement of the country’s climate targets, including the development of renewable energy sources. The Framework sets out which projects are eligible for ‘green financing’, in line with international standards (such as the ICMA’s Green Bond Principles 2021).

name: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan
description: The National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan is a framework to guide the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity and associated ecosystems in Zimbabwe from 2015 to 2020. It provides actions and strategies for ecosystem-based climate change mitigation and adaptation.

name: Regulation on Ozone-Depleting Substances
description: This document seeks to enforce regulating mechanisms on the use and destruction of substances that deplete the ozone layer. It is enlisted as one of the relevant laws contributing to climate change mitigation in Turkey’s 2023 Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC).

name: Electricity Act
Just Transition Framework for South Africa
description: At its Sixth Meeting held on 27 May 2022, the Presidential Climate Commission (PCCC) adopted the Just Transition Framework. A final version was published in July 2022, with policy recommendations. According to the PCC, the Just Transition Framework is a planning tool for achieving a just transition in South Africa, setting out the actions that the government and its social partners will take to achieve a just transition, and the outcomes to be realised in the short, medium, and long term. The Just Transition Framework is organised into seven main actions: (1) Foundations on which the framework builds; (2) Definition of a Just Transition for South Africa; (3) Principles to guide the transition; (4) At-risk sectors and value chains; (5) Key policy areas to give effect to the transition; (6) Effective governance arrangements; (7) Financing a Just Transition.

name: Resolution 156/ 2014 from the National Water Resources Council
description: It establishes guidelines for education capacity building, social mobilization, information and communication for perception of risks and vulnerabilities, and prevention, mitigation and increase resilience to water-related disasters.

name: Law No. 121 on offshore wind energy
description: In May 2024, Romania adopted its first offshore wind energy law. The law creates the legislative framework to develop offshore wind projects in the Romanian Black Sea.

name: Decree 2015-1850 of December 29, 2015 taken pursuant to Article L. 533-22-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code
description: This Decree replaces Article D. 533-16-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code. It elaborates on the standard of information that entities and portfolio management companies, to which the Code applies, must disclose around their ESG investment policies. Article 1.III states that the criteria related to environmental objectives must include an assessment of physical and transition risks, and an assessment of the entity's progress towards achieving the objectives of the energy and ecological transition (set out in Article L. 533-22.1 of the Monetary Code).

name: Plan of Phase out or Reconversion of Coal Units
description: This policy document from the Ministry of Eenergy sets out the outcomes of the Phase Out and/ or Reconversion of Coal Units Roundtable" and the resulting "Zero Carbon Energy Agreement" reached between the Ministry of Energy and coal-fired power plant owners in 2019. The document lays out plans for further roundtable meetings every 5 years to set further phase out schedules.

name: Carbon Management Strategy
description: In February 2024, Germany approves a new carbon management strategy, setting out the use of CCS / CCU.

name: Monetary and Financial Code
description: Article L533-22-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code of France was modified with the passage of France's Law 2015-992 in 2015. In the current version of Article L533-22-1, which has been in force since March 2021, portfolio management companies must include information on the risks associated with climate change (as well as on risks linked to biodiversity), as part of their compliance with the obligations set out in Article 3 of the EU Regulation 2022/1288, which contains the technical standards financial market participants must be when disclosing sustainability-related information under the Sustainable Finance Disclosures Regulation (SFDR). If companies choose not to publish certain pieces of information in their statements, they must justify why they have not done so.

name: National Water Basin Management Strategy 2014-2023
description: This strategy aims to improve watershed management and biodiversity conservation, by preventing environmental degradation in water catchment basins, promoting effective agricultural practices, and developing a biodiversity monitoring system. It further seeks to integrate climate change mitigation and adaptation strategies in water basin management to increase resilience against climate-change related disasters.

name: Anti-greenwashing rule
description: The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) Handbook includes an 'anti-greenwashing rule' (ESG 4.3.1R), which applies to all communications that mention sustainability-linked characteristics of products or services available for clients in the UK by FCA-authorised firms. The rule tooke ffect from 31 May 2024.

name: Commercial Code
description: Article L225-102-1 of France's Commercial Code includes provisions on non-financial disclosure obligations for companies to which the Code applies. Companies that exceed certain thresholds set by the Council of State (in Article L 225-100), are required to produce a declaration of extra-financial performance in their management reports. Companies that are mentioned in article L. 233-16 are required to publish a consolidated statement of their extra-financial performance exceed certain thresholds, also set by decree in the Council of State. The declaration must include particular information relating to the impact of the company on climate change (as well as the company's social commitments on sustainable development, the circular economy, measures to reduce food waste and to reduce food insecurity, as well as other SDG and ESG linked measures). The information the company must provide relating to its climate change impacts must include direct and indirect greenhouse gas emissions linked to transport activities upstream and downstream of the company's activities (scope 3 emissions) and must be accompanied by an action plan aimed at reducing these emissions (in particular, through the use of rail and river-based transport methods, as well as biofuels with a low carbon footprint, and electromobility).

name: Law on Spatial Planning and Construction 2013, amended in 2019
description: This law outlines the methodological approach to designing spatial planning documents, with a focus on climate change. It encourages energy-efficient building, inclusion of bio-climactic factors in location selection of buildings, and consideration of protective measures against natural disasters and technical failures.

name: Decree on the Types of Activities and Gases with a Greenhouse Effect
description: This Decree is based on the provisions of Serbia’s Law on Climate Change. It specifies the types of greenhouse gases (GHG) and greenhouse gas emitting activities required to obtain permits and submit monitoring plans. It further determines types of aviation activities for which permits and monitoring plans are not mandatory.

name: Decree no. 20 - National Forestry Strategy 2018 - 2050
description: This Decree approves the National Forestry Strategy 2018-20150, which aims to increase forest cover, stimulate the sustainable forestry industry, conserve Panama’s forest heritage as an important basis for ecosystems and mitigate the effects of climate change.

name: Regulation on Fuel Economy Data and CO2 Emissions for New Passenger Vehicles
description: This regulation is based on the provisions of the Serbian Law for Climate Change. It seeks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and air pollutants by regulating the label content, model, and promotional materials of new passenger vehicles in the Republic of Serbia.

name: National Home Retrofit Scheme 2020 (One Stop Shop Development Call)
description: This scheme is aimed at engaging groups of private households, registered Housing Associations and Local Authorities and Energy Utilities or other organisations who wish to participate in delivering a “One Stop Shop” type service for energy efficiency works.

name: Law on power market
description: The present law was signed by the Polish President in December 2017. The law aims at enhancing the security of electricity supply and new energy capacity sources, especially renewables. The law introduces a market-wide capacity mechanism. Generation and demand-response capacity providers will be able to receive remuneration for their availability to generate electricity or to reduce their electricity consumption.

name: National Security Strategy 2018
description: The National Security Strategy builds on the National Security Policy 2017-2022 to implement necessary changes, including on climate change aspects. It integrates the State’s major security policies, goals, responsibilities and courses of action into a roadmap or blueprint for the fulfilment of the national security vision.

name: Green hydrogen roadmap
description: This document aims at fostering the production and use of green hydrogen in Spain. The government announced that it will invest 1.5 billion euros by 2023 to foster the production of renewable-energy-sourced hydrogen in the country.

name: Suriname National REDD+ Strategy
description: This document aims to protect Suriname's forests and enhance its carbon storage facilities.

name: The Electricity Proclamation (No. 86-1997)
description: The proclamation establishes the Ethiopian Electricity Agency (EEA) as an autonomous federal government organ (later changed to Ethiopian Energy Agency). The Agency's mandate is to regulate the operation of the energy sector on technical and economic issues - from standards, efficiency and reliability, to tariffs.

name: National climate change strategy for the waste sector 2021
description:
The vision of the National Climate Change Strategy for the Waste Sector is to effectively and sustainably manage solid and liquid waste in all of Madagascar's communes by strengthening the institutional, organisational and legal framework, building capacity for the implementation of the UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement at national level, and improving the quality of waste management.
In line with the commitments made by the Malagasy government, the strategy has 6 priority areas:

Strengthen the institutional arrangement and the legal and regulatory framework for the waste sector, by taking account of the climate change dimension
Implementation of a capacity-building plan for all stakeholders involved in greenhouse gas inventories, the data collection and management system, waste recovery and reporting
Development of a data exchange flow mechanism through the promotion of inter ministerial collaboration
Strengthen the monitoring and evaluation system
Establishment of a sustainable funding and budget programming mechanism
Implementation of a skills and technology transfer mechanism

name: Decree 786/04
description: This document creates the Offices of Climate Change and Clean Development Mechanism.

name: National Strategy for REDD+ 2017-2030 (ENAREDD+)
description: This document sets Mexico's strategy to protect its forests.

name: Act on Renewable Energy Sources ('RES Act', Dz.U. 2015 poz. 478)
The National Strategy on Adaptation to Climate Change 2022-2030 (First version)
description:
The National Strategy on Adaptation to Climate Change for the period 2022- 2030 to 2050 (SNASC) and the National Action Plan for implementation of the National Strategy on Adaptation to Climate Change (NSSAC) focus on adaptation strategies in the following sectors/areas:

Forests
Biodiversity and ecosystem services
Population, public health and air quality
Education and awareness
Cultural heritage
Urban systems
Agriculture and rural development
Energy
Transport
Tourism
Industry

name: Disclosure Standards for ESG funds
description: These Standards require an ESG-related fund to disclose its ESG objectives and the standards and processes used to select the underlying ESG investments.

name: National Employment Policy
description: The National Employment Policy aims to improve the employment opportunities in Fiji to cope with socio-economic developments as well as climate change and natural disasters. The policy places emphasis on a just transition for the work force in the context of climate change by identifying and promoting green jobs and new green skill sets.

name: Botswana Integrated Water Resources Management & Water Efficiency Plan
description: As a semi-arid country, Botswana experiences drought years which are intensified by climate change and fresh-water supply issues. The plan therefore uses integrated solutions for water resources management, which were developed through stakeholder consultations. The resulting strategic areas are for example efficiency of water allocation; or water supply and demand management.

name: National Hydrogen Strategy
description: The government approved its hydrogen strategy in May 2020.

name: Action Plan to Reduce CO2 Emissions from Brazilian Civil Aviation
description: This action plan establishes a permanent Working Group within the National Civil Aviation Secretariat to coordinate activities related to the preparation of the Action Plan to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from civil aviation.

name: National Disaster Risk Management Plan (NDRMP) 2009
description: The National Disaster Risk Management Plan provides a framework for sectors and stakeholders to prepare disaster risk reduction and emergency management plans for natural and man-made hazards and vulnerabilities. Climate change is considered as a major phenomenon that intensifies the frequency of disasters and thus features strongly in the report.

name: Decree of December 10, 2021 creating a program as part of the system of energy savings certificates
description: This decree extends the Advenir programme to 2025 and sets new funds and targets for new charging points.

name: Directive 2023/2413 (Renewable Energy Directive) amending Directive (EU) 2018/2001 on the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources, Supplementing Regulation 2019/807 and Commission Implementing Regulation 2022/996
description: This document establishes a common framework for the promotion of energy from renewable sources. It sets a binding Union target for the overall share of energy from renewable sources in the Union's gross final consumption of energy in 2030. It also lays down rules on financial support for electricity from renewable sources, on self-consumption of such electricity, on the use of energy from renewable sources in the heating and cooling sector and in the transport sector, on regional cooperation between Member States, and between Member States and third countries, on guarantees of origin, on administrative procedures and on information and training. It also establishes sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions saving criteria for biofuels, bioliquids and biomass fuels. Supplementing Regulation 2019/807 lays down the criteria for determining high indirect land-use change-risk feedstock for which a significant expansion of the production area into land with high carbon stock is observed and the certification of low indirect land-use change-risk biofuels, bioliquids and biomass fuels.As part of the EU's 'Fit for 55' package, a legislative package that aims to align the EU's climate, energy, land use, transport, and taxation policies with a GHG emissions reduction target of 55% by 2030 (compared with 1990 levels), this Directive has been reformed to set an overall binding renewable energy target of at least 42.5% in the EU's energy mix by 2030, while aiming for a target of 45%. Among the most important updates to the Directive are new provisions on bioenergy, targeted at preventing the degradation of carbon sinks and biodiversity loss associated with existing practices.

name: Botswana Eleventh National Development Plan
description: Botswana's NDPs are grand scheme policy frameworks, which define the country's medium-term development goals and strategies. The current plan started in April 2017 and runs until March 2023. The 11th NDP is the second of its kind to incorporate a results-based approach. Contrary to the 10th plan, the current document, the current plan does refer to climate change as a more explicit issue, and formulates two priorities: sustainable human settlements, and financing of sustainable environment progmrammes. In the transport sector, the plan details its capacity with regard to biodiesel. The plan lists several climate change relevant initiatives and programmes in the forestry and energy sectors, including: the Community-Based Natural Resource Management Programme and the Renewable Energy-Based Rural Electrification Programme.

name: Liberia National Vision 2030
description: This document aims to formulate a shared, long-term national and global vision for Liberia. The stated 'building blocks' of the vision are: economic prosperity; social and demographic harmony; democracy; environmental protection; cultural vibrance; and technological innovation.

name: Ordinance 65/2014 approving the Regulations for crop insurance and loss compensation, integrated into the Integrated System of Protection against adverse climate events
description: This ordinance approves tegulations on crop insurance and loss compensation, integrated into the Integrated System for the Protection against adverse climate events (SIPAC), approved by Decree-Law no. 23/2000, of 2 March.

name: Emergency Decree 320/2023
description: This decree introduces a carbon tax for Hungary’s 40 largest emitters. This tax penalises the trade in ETS credits.

name: National Economic and Social Development Plan 2016-2020
description: The 2016-2020 National Economic and Social Development Plan (PNDES) constitutes the second generation of plan. It aims to operationalise over the period 2016-2020, the Vision of an emerging and prosperous Guinea by 2040.

name: Directive (EU) 2024/1760 of the European Parliament and of the Council (the 'Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive' or 'CSDDD')
